summary: Two players each pilot a unique deck of iconic characters, moving on a point-to-point map and resolving fights by simultaneously revealing attack/defense cards with tactical boosts and combos, so combat feels like a tense card-based duel rather than dice luck. Matches are fast (20-40 min), highly asymmetric, and reward learning each hero's specific deck quirks and counters.
praised: Deep asymmetry between characters despite simple core rules
No-luck, card-based combat that rewards reading your opponent
Fast setup and playtime, easy to teach the basic loop
High production value miniatures and board art
Great replayability from mixing heroes across different sets
criticised: Miniatures add cost/hype but don't affect gameplay, seen as unnecessary bling by some
Some hero match-ups feel imbalanced, especially early sets before errata
4-player free-for-all/team mode is less tight than 1v1
Overwhelming and expensive to collect as the line expanded across many sets

scoring.why: The game ends the instant one side's characters are all reduced to zero health, so there is no scoring at all beyond elimination

_name: Unmatched: Battle of Legends, Volume One
